_note: Reviewed corrections to Gemma-generated notes. Each was found by reading the note against the original in vault/raw/. Ingest applies them after generation (greedy decoding makes the generated text reproducible) and warns if one no longer matches. note='*' applies to every note (used for 'why' lines that appear on both ends of a link). The originals are never changed.

corrections.reason: misleading: bias comes from choosing the max of 81 noisy estimates, not from held-out seeds (source lines 263-266)
corrections.find: The selected checkpoint mean of 1660.0 is optimistically biased due to held-out seeds.
corrections.replace: The selected checkpoint's held-out mean of 1660.0 is optimistically biased because it is the best of 81 noisy estimates; the reported 1360.0 is unbiased because its seeds were never used to choose.

corrections.reason: misleading: the source says the loss IS a temporal-difference error, which is why a rising loss is not a bad sign (lines 153-159)
corrections.find: The loss went up during the fastest improvement period, indicating a temporal-difference error
corrections.replace: The loss went up during the fastest improvement period; because it is a temporal-difference error whose targets rise as the agent improves, that is not a bad sign

corrections.reason: garbled menu path (lines 36-37)
corrections.find: To open in Google Colab, select Runtime to Change runtime type to T4 GPU and Run all.
corrections.replace: In Google Colab, select Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU, then Runtime → Run all.

corrections.reason: the proposal is an annealing schedule, stated as a next experiment (lines 316-317)
corrections.find: Change exploration decay from 1.0 to 0.05 over the first 200,000 decisions instead of fixing it at 0.10.
corrections.replace: The proposed next experiment anneals exploration from 1.0 to 0.05 over the first ~200,000 decisions instead of fixing it at 0.10.

corrections.reason: it is the README's prediction, not a test result (lines 326-329)
corrections.find: This test predicts a higher ceiling rather than faster early progress.
corrections.replace: The README predicts the change would show up as a higher ceiling rather than faster early progress.

corrections.reason: the next experiment is a proposal, not something that was done (lines 316-317)
corrections.find: — Change exploration from 1.0 to 0.05 over 200,000 decisions instead of fixing it at 0.10.
corrections.replace: — Exploration was held constant at 0.10; the proposed next experiment anneals it from 1.0 to 0.05 over ~200,000 decisions.

corrections.reason: vague: which seeds (lines 265-266)
corrections.find: while the reported 1360.0 is not biased because certain seeds were never used.
corrections.replace: while the reported 1360.0 is not, because its evaluation seeds were never used to choose the checkpoint.

corrections.reason: inverted: app_user exists so the app can NOT bypass RLS; it lacks BYPASSRLS and does not own the table (lines 317-324)
corrections.find: The `app_user` role is used by the application because it does not own the contacts table, which is required to bypass RLS restrictions.
corrections.replace: The backend connects as a dedicated `app_user` role without `BYPASSRLS` that does not own the contacts table, because the default `neondb_owner` bypassed RLS and left the policies inert.

corrections.reason: wrong flow: the SPA signs in against Neon Auth directly, then calls the API with a bearer token (lines 147-151)
corrections.find: The React SPA interacts with the Express API to manage authentication.
corrections.replace: The React SPA signs in directly against Neon Auth, then calls the Express API with the session token as a bearer token.

corrections.reason: the client, not the auth service, sends the token (line 268)
corrections.find: Sign-up and sign-in use Neon Managed Better Auth, which sends an opaque session token on every API request.
corrections.replace: Sign-up and sign-in use Neon Managed Better Auth; the client then sends the opaque session token as a bearer token on every API request.

corrections.reason: imprecise: the tests check that no statement matches rows on id alone (line 388)
corrections.find: Isolation tests verify that database operations are scoped by user_id and prevent direct ID matching.
corrections.replace: Isolation tests verify that every select, update and delete is scoped by user_id and never matches rows on id alone.

corrections.reason: imprecise: the ceiling was at 2 layers (lines 53-56)
corrections.find: Adding teaching material did not raise the ceiling; it moved failures around in lower layer runs.
corrections.replace: At 2 layers, adding targeted teaching material did not raise the ceiling; it moved failures around.

corrections.reason: no context for 'bolded files' (lines 246-249)
corrections.find: The three bolded files are the two-clause analogy frame, missing combination, and plural structure.
corrections.replace: Three corpus files changed after E2: the two-clause analogy frame (file 08), the missing 'happens after … the earlier meal is' combination (file 05), and 'the {plural} are …' (file 01).

corrections.reason: wrong verb: the chat used the E5 model (lines 631-634)
corrections.find: The model was rendered from llm_runs/20260922T021637_203555Z/model.pt.
corrections.replace: The chat evidence used the experiment 5 model (llm_runs/20260922T021637_203555Z/model.pt: 4 layers, 230,848 parameters).

corrections.find: Installation involves python3.12 and pip to install numpy from requirements.txt.
corrections.replace: Setup creates a Python 3.12 virtual environment and installs requirements.txt plus numpy.

corrections.reason: the per-domain lookup table is what the proposed experiment would test, not a conclusion (lines 767-780)
corrections.find: The limitation lang_39 cannot be fixed by teaching, suggesting a per-domain lookup table.
corrections.replace: lang_39 cannot be fixed by teaching because its tested sentence is an eval prompt; the proposed next experiment tests whether a before/after rule taught on non-vehicle examples transfers.

corrections.reason: off-topic: these two sentences are about exploration, not replay (they belong to Exploration Rate)
corrections.find: Another experiment involved changing the exploration setting to anneal epsilon from 1.0 to 0.05 over the first ~200,000 decisions instead of fixing it at 0.10 ([[Pac-Man DQN README#My next experiment|S2]]). This was done because a constant 0.10 is a compromise that is wrong at both ends of training ([[Pac-Man DQN README#My next experiment|S2]]).
corrections.replace: The shipped 5,000-transition buffer held only about eight games, so sampled batches came from a handful of highly correlated recent episodes; 50,000 holds about 80 games ([[Pac-Man DQN README#My three choices|S1]]).
